newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision buys NY area systems from TCI.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision buys NY area systems from TCI.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp. said on Monday it will buy 10 cable television systems in the New York area from Tele-Communications Inc. for about $422.4 million in stock.
Cablevision, the sixth-largest cable operator in the United States, will get 820,000 new customers and give the nation's largest cable TV company 12.2 million shares of Cablevision Class A stock.

That would give TCI a 33 percent stake in Cablevision, which will continue to be controlled by the family of Cablevision CEO James Dolan. TCI will get two seats on Cablevision's board, the companies said.
Cablevision will also assume about $669 million of TCI debt associated with cable systems in New Jersey, Long Island and New York's Rockland and Westchester counties.

The deals brings Cablevision's total number of New York area customers to 2.5 million from 1.7 million. It said it plans to have more than 100 channels on all of its New York area cable systems in the next two years and will also move to high-speed data transmission (HDTV).
Shares of Cablevision, which owns systems in 19 states, closed Friday at $34.625 on the American Stock Exchange.
